name: Glycomacropeptide (casein glycomacropeptide)
short: In children with PKU, the residual phenylalanine in glycomacropeptide raised blood phenylalanine in two trials. Gut symptoms were similar or better than with amino acid formulas.
text: Human safety data come from small trials in people with phenylketonuria (PKU), where glycomacropeptide is used as a protein substitute. Because it contains a small amount of phenylalanine, blood phenylalanine was higher with it than with phenylalanine-free amino acid formulas in children: by a mean of 114 μmol/L in a 12-week crossover trial in 12 children aged 4 to 9, and in a crossover study in 19 children of glycomacropeptide supplemented with amino acids, where the authors said its residual phenylalanine increased blood phenylalanine concentration. In a 3-week crossover trial in 30 people with PKU aged 15 to 49, plasma phenylalanine did not rise significantly despite higher phenylalanine intake, participants reported improved gastrointestinal symptoms and less hunger, and the authors described it as safe and acceptable. In the trial in children, stomach pain, heartburn and reflux, and wind and bloating improved with glycomacropeptide. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
